title: scheduler-label-flap-slow-eviction-incident-log
content:
Summary:

On 2024-11-04 we observed a ~40 minute window where a subset of nodes in prod-eu-1 experienced large numbers of PodBackOff / CrashLoopBackOff and slow, cascading evictions. Impact was concentrated on inference-serving ReplicaSets with many small ephemeral pods (seq-length=256 workloads). Overall request success rate dropped ~9% and P50 latency rose ~15ms for affected models.

Unusual aspects: the scheduler continued to bind pods to nodes that were reporting transient network path issues to the control plane (kubelet->apiserver RPCs), while the kubelet on those nodes did not immediately trigger hard evictions. This produced a stretched-out eviction curve and more application-level retries.

High-level timeline (UTC):
- 2024-11-04T08:09:10: Alert: pod restarts spike on prod-eu-1 (alerts/pods.restart-rate > 30m baseline)
- 2024-11-04T08:12:22: First SRE on-call paged; began collection (kubectl get nodes -o wide, kubelet logs)
- 2024-11-04T08:15:00: Observed repeated rc=504 errors between kubelet and apiserver in node journal (systemd)
- 2024-11-04T08:17:30: kube-scheduler logs show several "FailedPredicate: InsufficientMemory" for pods that were later scheduled on the same node after label updates
- 2024-11-04T08:21:10: CNI agent on nodes reported route cache TTL invalidation; logs show intermittent "failed to program route" with EALREADY at 5s intervals
- 2024-11-04T08:25:00: Several node labels were observed to flip between maintenance:pending and maintenance:active due to a flaky automation (labeler service) retry behavior
- 2024-11-04T08:35:40: First mitigation: scaled down best-effort replicas for noisy inference jobs and drained 2 nodes with the highest restart counts
- 2024-11-04T08:49:00: Traffic largely recovered after node drains and restarting the labeler service; remaining tail evictions subsided by 08:56

Signals examined:
- kubelet journal: repeated rpc timeout to apiserver: "dial tcp <apiserver-ip>:443: i/o timeout" correlated with route programming failures in CNI logs
- CNI (calico) logs: route-programming errors with message "failed to program route: file exists (EEXIST)" followed by a burst of ARP cache churn on the same nodes
- kube-scheduler: predicate failures referencing node labels and taints; binding occurs after label flips due to labeler retries
- node metrics: memory_available showed a sudden drop on 3 nodes concurrent with increased ephemeral ephemeral-storage usage; inode pressure was not present
- apiserver audit: several label updates from labeler-service (service account: labeler@infra) retried in rapid succession (exponential backoff misconfigured)
- application-level: liveness probes returning 503 during brief pauses in network reachability to dependencies (config store)

Root cause hypothesis (contributing factors):
1) Labeler automation bug: labeler-service retried label updates without jitter/backoff which caused rapid oscillation of a maintenance label. Oscillation changed scheduler predicates and caused some controllers to move pods repeatedly.
2) CNI route programming race: when label-flap coincided with routine route reconciliation, the CNI attempted to program overlapping routes and returned EEXIST/EALREADY rather than deduplicating properly. This pushed the nodes' dataplane into intermittent packet loss while the agent retried.
3) Kubelet->apiserver transient connectivity: the intermittent packet loss caused RPC timeouts that delayed kubelet's eviction decision window (kubelet's eviction thresholds stayed momentarily below hard eviction), so pods lingered in unhealthy state and restarted more slowly.
4) Pod QoS distribution: several inference jobs ran as Guaranteed/Burstable with small resource reservations so scheduler packed them onto impacted nodes; combined with autoscaler pacing this amplified the blast radius.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Disabled labeler-service (rolled back to earlier image) at 2024-11-04T08:28:00 to stop further label oscillation (owner: infra/automation)
- Drained and cordoned two worst-affected nodes to expedite allocation to healthy nodes (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data)
- Increased CNI agent logging level and restarted calico/node on affected hosts to force fresh route reconciliation
- Scaled down noisy inference ReplicaSets by 30% as a rapid load reduction

Investigation artifacts and useful commands used during triage:
- kubectl get events --all-namespaces --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Pod -n prod-eu-1 | grep Evicted
- journalctl -u kubelet -o short-iso | sed -n '1,400p' > /tmp/node1-kubelet.log
- kubectl describe node node-eu-12 | egrep -i 'Pressure|Conditions|Taint'
- calicoctl node status --details
- grep -iE "failed to program route|EEXIST|EALREADY|route" /var/log/calico/node.log | tail -n 200
- kubectl get pods -o custom-columns='NAME:metadata.name,NODE:spec.nodeName,RESTARTS:status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount' --all-namespaces | sort -k3 -n -r | head -n 50

Monitoring and dashboards to consult for future triage:
- k8s.kubelet.rpc_timeouts (per node)
- calico.route.failures (per node, last 1m/5m/30m)
- scheduler.bind_success_rate (per node and per label group)
- pod.restart_rate by deployment
- controlplane.packetloss_percent via cluster eBPF collector

Runbook updates proposed (short term):
- Add a gating policy for labeler-service that ensures label updates to node metadata are applied with linear backoff + jitter and a per-node rate limit (owner: infra/automation)
- CNI: add dedupe logic on route programming errors; ensure CNI returns idempotent success for duplicate route attempts (owner: infra-networking)
- Kubelet: add a small e2e test that simulates route program failures so eviction path and RPC timeout behavior is exercised (owner: eng-sre)
- Scheduling policy: avoid hard packing of low-memory inference jobs by adding a soft-affinity and spread constraint for critical ReplicaSets (owner: platform-engineering)

Longer-term actions (priority ordered):
1) Implement labeler-service canary with rate limits and circuit-breaker (Q1 2025)
2) Calico upgrade to include idempotent route API (evaluate 3rd party patch, Q1 2025)
3) Add control-plane eBPF-based packetloss alert that correlates with kubelet rpc errors (Q1 2025)
4) Revisit autoscaler pacing to avoid simultaneous large reschedules when nodes are flapping (Q2 2025)

Open questions to resolve:
- Why did kubelet eviction heuristics not trigger earlier given RPC timeouts? Need to capture kubelet memory and disk eviction thresholds timeline per node during the event.
- Can we reproduce the route-programming EEXIST condition in a lab with our current calico version?
- Is labeler-service the only automation updating maintenance-related labels, or are there other systems (Ansible/baremetal scripts) that could contribute?

Owner list and action assignments (tentative):
- infra/automation (Aisha Raman): fix labeler retry logic, add canary and rate-limit (owner)
- infra-networking (Diego Morales): reproduce route programming race, propose calico patch or config change (owner)
- eng-sre (Evan Liu): create kubelet evicton timeline capture playbook + incident runbook additions (owner)
- platform-engineering (Priya Desai): schedule policy change to add soft-spread for inference ReplicaSets (owner)

Notes for postmortem write-up:
- Include timeline with exact audit log extracts for label updates and calico errors
- Quantify user impact by model and zone (SLA hit calculations)
- Capture root causal chain focusing on automation + dataplane race conditions rather than single-point failure

Appendix - short reproducibility checklist for lab:
- Deploy a 3-node calico cluster with same calico version as prod-eu-1
- Run a background task that rapidly toggles a node label via the k8s API to simulate labeler oscillation
- Instrument calico route programming to occasionally return EEXIST artificially (via small wrapper or fault-injection)
- Observe kubelet rpc timeouts and pod lifecycle behaviour under the induced dataplane churn

Quick copies of relevant logs (redacted):
- calico/node.log excerpt: "2024-11-04T08:21:10Z ERROR failed to program route: vxlan0: route exists (EEXIST) pod=prod/inf-abc"
- kubelet journal excerpt: "2024-11-04T08:15:02Z WARN kubelet: failed to POST status: rpc error: context deadline exceeded"
- kube-scheduler excerpt: "E1104 08:17:30.234 scheduler: predicate failed for node-eu-12: node(s) didn't match node selectors: maintenance!=active"

I will convert this draft into a formal incident report if the working group agrees with the causal chain. For now, keeping as working notes and proposed actions.

Last edited by: Aisha Raman on 2024-11-12
